Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:12:1.hebrew: שמור לי ואשמור לך שומר שכר - וחייב אם נגנבה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:12:1.english: "Safeguard for me and I will safeguard for you" – a paid bailee - and he is liable if [the item] is stolen:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:12:2.hebrew: ואמאי שמירה בבעלים היא - בעליו של חפץ זה שנגנב במלאכתו של שומר היה, שאף הוא משמר היה לו. וכתיב (שמות כב, יד): "אם בעליו עמו לא ישלם", ודרשינן לקמן "עמו" – במלאכתו. ואע"ג דבשואל כתיב, לקמן דרשינן ליה נמי אכולהו שומרין בפרק השואל (לקמן בבא מציעא ד' צה.):
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:12:2.english: But why? It is safeguarding with the owners - The owner of this item that was stolen was in the service of the bailee, as he [the bailee] also had him safeguard [his own property]. And it is written (Exodus 22:14): "If its owner is with it, he shall not pay," and we expound below that "with him" means in his work. And although [this verse] is written regarding a borrower, below we also expound it as applying to all bailees, in the chapter [entitled] HaSho'el (below, Bava Metzia 95a):

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:12:3.english: And I will safeguard for you tomorrow - for now he is not in his work:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:13:1.hebrew: השאילני ואשאיל לך - אין זה שואל להתחייב באונסין, שאין כל הנאה שלו, שאף הוא משאילו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:13:1.english: Lend me and I will lend you - This one is not [considered] a borrower, [so as] to be liable for unavoidable accidents, since the entire benefit is not his, for he too lends to him:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:13:2.hebrew: שמירה בבעלים היא - הא דקאמר "אשמור לי ואשמור לך" קאי עליה, ששניהם שומרים זה במלאכתו של זה. אבל הא דקאמר "השאילני כליך ואני אשאיל לך כליי", "שמור לי ואשאילך" או "השאילני ואשמור לך", אין כאן בעלים של חפץ במלאכתו של שומר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:13:2.english: It is safeguarding with the owners - [The case of] "Safeguard for me and I will safeguard for you" is the one to which [the question] applies, since both of them [are working] in each other's service. But [in the cases of] "Lend me your vessels and I will lend you my vessels," "Safeguard for me and I will lend to you," or "Lend to me and I will safeguard for you," there is no owner of the object [engaged] in the work of the bailee:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:14:1.hebrew: אהלויי - מוכרי אהל, שמכבסים בו בגדים, והוא עשב. ואיכא דאמרי: אהלות, והוא מין בושם:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:14:1.english: Ahaluyei - Sellers of ahal [ice plant], with which they launder clothes, and it is a [type of] herb. And there are those who say [the word is] ahalot, which is a kind of perfume:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:14:2.hebrew: זיל ואפי לן - קס"ד שהאפייה יומא דידיה הוה, דהשתא לא הוו אינהו בשמירת טליתו אלא כשומרי חנם, ואצטריך למימר "פשעו בה", דאי לא פשעו לא מיחייבי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:14:2.english: Go and bake for us - The initial assumption is that it was his [own] day [to bake], since now they [the others] were guarding his cloak only as unpaid custodians, and it was necessary to say "they were negligent with it," because if they had not been negligent, they would not be liable.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:15:1.hebrew: פשיעה בבעלים - שאף הוא במלאכתן היה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:15:1.english: Negligence while with the owners - For he too [the bailee, i.e., the owner of the cloak] was engaged in their work [at the time of the theft]:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:15:2.hebrew: איגלאי מילתא דההיא שעתא שכרא הוה שתי - ולא היה במלאכתן, שעדיין לא התחיל לאפות, ונמצא שבשעה שנעשו הן שומרין לא מסר עצמו להיות מלאכתן עליו. אבל אם נתעסק מיד ואפה, ולאחר שאפה שתי שכרא, ובאותה שעה אבדה טליתו, פשיעה בבעלים נמי הויא, הואיל וכשנעשו שומרין היה במלאכתן, דאמרינן לקמן (בבא מציעא ד' צה:): היה עמו בשעת שאלה, אינו צריך להיות עמו בשעת שבורה ומתה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:15:2.english: It was discovered that at that time he was drinking beer - and he was not engaged in their work, for he had not yet begun to bake. Thus, at the moment they became bailees, he had not committed himself to having their work be upon him. But had he immediately busied himself and baked, and only after baking drunk beer, and at that time his cloak was lost, it would also be negligence while [the bailee is] with the owner, since when they became bailees he was engaged in their work. For we say below (Bava Metzia 95b): If he was with him at the time of the borrowing, he does not need to be with him at the time of [the animal's] breaking a limb or dying:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:16:1.hebrew: הניחא למאן דאמר - בפרק השואל (שם.) פשיעה בבעלים פטור, היינו דאיכסיף:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:16:1.english: This works out well according to the one who says - in the chapter [entitled] HaShoel (there), that [for] negligence while with the owners [the bailee] is exempt, that is why he was embarrassed:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:16:2.hebrew: אלא למאן דאמר פשיעה בבעלים חייב - שלא נאמרה הלכה פטור בבעלים אלא בשואל ושומר שכר, שחיובן בלא פשיעה. אבל שומר חנם, שחיובו אינו אלא בפשיעה, אינו פטור משום "בעליו עמו", הואיל ופשע. אמאי איכסיף:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:16:2.english: But according to the one who says that negligence while with the owners [makes one] liable - [This is because] the rule of exemption when [the bailee is working] with the owners was stated only regarding a borrower and a paid bailee, whose liability [applies] even without negligence. But an unpaid bailee, whose liability is only for negligence, is not exempt on account of "its owner is with him," since he was negligent. Why, then, was [Rav Pappa] embarrassed?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:16:3.hebrew: בההוא אגרא וכו' - והוו להו שומרי שכר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:16:3.english: As payment, etc. - And they were [thereby] paid bailees:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:1:1.hebrew: הא גמרתיו שומר שכר - ולא אמרינן: כיון שידעו הבעלים שכלו ימי האומנות ולא שלחו והביאום, פטור השומר. וגבי השואל נמי, אף על פי שידעו הבעלים שכלו ימי השאילה, שואל הוא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:1:1.english: [If he says,] "I completed it," he is a paid bailee - And we do not say: Since the owners knew that the days of the work had ended, and they did not send and bring them [back], the bailee is exempt. And likewise regarding a borrower, even though the owners knew that the days of the loan had ended, he is [still] a borrower [and remains liable]:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:1:2.hebrew: לא - תידק מהמשנה: הא דקאמר "גמרתיו", שומר שכר הוא? לא, אלא הכי דייק מינה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:1:2.english: No - You should [not] deduce [from the Mishnah] that [if he said] "I completed it," he is a paid bailee. Rather, this is how one should deduce from it:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:1:3.hebrew: הא הבא מעות - דגלי אדעתא דתפיס ליה אאגריה, שומר שכר הוא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:1:3.english: But [this:] "Bring money" - [This is] because he revealed his intention that he is holding it [as security] for his wages; [therefore] he is a paid bailee:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:2:1.hebrew: אבל גמרתיו מאי שומר חנם - דכל כמה דלא גלי דעתיה, ולית לן למימר דתפס ליה אאגריה, כלתה שמירת שכר פעולה מדגמריה ואודעיה. וגבי שואל נמי כלתה שמירת שאלה מדידעו הבעלים שכלו ימי השאלה, דהתם לאו לאודועי בעי, דהא ידע שלכך וכך ימים השאילה לו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:2:1.english: But [if he said] "I completed it," what [is the law]? Is he an unpaid bailee? - For as long as he has not revealed his intention, and we have no basis to say that he has seized it against his wages, [he is still a paid bailee]. The paid bailee's responsibility of a worker ends once he has completed [the work] and informed [the owner]. And regarding a borrower too, the responsibility of borrowing ends once the owners know that the days of the loan have ended, for there [with a borrower] there is no need to inform [the owner], since [the owner] already knows that he lent it to him for such-and-such a number of days:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:3:1.hebrew: שומר חנם נמי לא הוי - דאינו שומרו לו עוד, קאמר ליה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:3:1.english: He is not even an unpaid bailee - [One might think that] he said to him ["take what is yours"] [to mean] that he no longer guards it for him:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:3:2.hebrew: קמ"ל - דאינו תופסו על שכרו, הוא דקאמר ליה "טול את שלך", אבל מדין פקדון לא סליק נפשיה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:3:2.english: It teaches us - that he is not holding it [i.e., seizing it] for his wages; this is what he [the laborer] meant when he said to him ["Take what is yours"]. But from the law of a deposit, he has not removed himself [from responsibility]:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:4:1.hebrew: מאי לאו הוא הדין לגמרתיו - והאי דנקט "טול את שלך", לאשמועינן מינה דשומר חנם מיהת הוי, כדאמרן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:4:1.english: What, is it not the same [law] for "I have completed it" - And the fact that [the mishna] stated "take what is yours" is to teach us from it that he is, at any rate, an unpaid bailee, as we said:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:5:1.hebrew: וכן בשעה שמחזירה - כל כמה דלא אמר ליה לשואל משאיל "שלח", קמה ברשותיה דשואל, כי היכי דבשעת שאלה קיימא ברשות משאיל עד דאמר ליה שואל "שלח". וקס"ד דמשכלו ימי שאילה קאמר, דדמי לגמרתיו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:5:1.english: And similarly when he returns it - As long as the lender has not said to him [to the borrower], "Send [it]," the animal stands in the possession of the borrower, just as at the time of the loan it remains in the possession of the lender until the borrower says to him, "Send [it]." And the Gemara initially thought that [the mishna] is speaking of [a return] after the days of the loan have ended, since this is similar to [the case of] "I completed it [the work with it]."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:6:1.english: Exempt from [the liability of] a borrower - for [damage caused by] unavoidable accidents:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:6:2.english: And he is liable as a paid bailee - for theft and loss:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:6:3.english: Since he had benefit - from the borrowing:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:6:4.hebrew: מהני - להיות עליה על הפרה שומר שכר עד שתגיע ליד הבעלים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:6:4.english: He must provide benefit - by being a paid bailee over it [the cow] until it reaches the owner's possession:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:7:1.english: To send them to his father-in-law's house - [as] betrothal gifts to his betrothed:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:7:2.hebrew: כפי טובת הנאה - שיחזיקו לי טובה שפקדתים בסבלונות:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:7:2.english: In accordance with the benefit - that they will be grateful to me for having visited them with gifts:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:7:3.hebrew: ונאנסו בהליכה חייב - דהואיל וקצץ דמיהן ומשכן לשם לקיחה, הרי הם לקוחין בידו עד שידע שאינה לקוחה. והכי נמי אמרינן בהמוכר את הספינה (ב"ב דף פז:): אמר שמואל, הלוקח כלי מן האומן על מנת לבקרו, ואם אין בו מום יקחנו, ונאנס בידו - חייב, והוא דקיצי דמיה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:7:3.english: "And they were destroyed by accident on the way, he is liable" - Since he fixed their price and took them for the purpose of purchase, they are considered purchased in his hand until he knows that it is not purchased. And so too we say in [the chapter] "One who sells a ship" (Bava Batra 87b): Shmuel said, one who takes a vessel from an artisan on condition to inspect it, [saying] that if it has no defect he will buy it, and it was destroyed by accident while in his possession, is liable — and this applies when they fixed its price:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:8:1.hebrew: בחזירה פטור - מאונסין, מפני שהוא כנושא שכר בחזירה ולא כשואל. ומהו נשיאות שכרו? הואיל ונהנה שנתפאר בהן. והיינו כוותיה דאמימר, דאע"ג דיהיב ליה כפי טובת הנאה שבהן, הוי עלייהו שומר שכר אחר שכלתה שמירת המקח, הואיל ונהנה; כל שכן גבי שאלה, דלא יהיב ליה מידי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 81a:8:1.english: On the way back he is exempt - from [liability for] accidents, because on the return trip he is like a paid bailee and not like a borrower. And what is his payment [for bearing the item]? Since he derived benefit, in that he was adorned by them. And this is in accordance with Ameimar, who [held] that even though he gave him [payment] in proportion to the benefit [he received] from them, he is considered a paid bailee over them after the period of the sale's safekeeping has ended, since he benefited; all the more so in the case of a borrowing, where he did not give him anything:

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 81a:16:1.hebrew: הניחא למ"ד פשיעה בבעלים פטור - וקשיא למ"ד חייב מעובדא דרב פפא. והאמוראים דרב אחא ורבינא איפליגו בה לקמן, שהיו אחר רב פפא:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 81a:16:1.english: This works out well according to the one who says that negligence while with the owners is exempt - But it is difficult according to the one who says [the bailee is] liable, from the incident of Rav Pappa. [The Amoraim] Rav Acha and Ravina disagreed about it below, for they lived after Rav Pappa:

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 81a:1:1.hebrew: הא גמרתיו שומר שכר - וא"ת: ומאי פריך? שאני הכא דאכתי תפיס ליה אאגריה, ולכך הוי שומר שכר אף על פי שגמר מלאכתו! ומיהו לטעמיה דלעיל, דמדמינן אומן לשוכר, ולא אמרינן שאני אומן דתפיס ליה אאגריה, פריך הכא שפיר. וי"ל דלא מהני תפיס ליה אאגריה אלא דוקא בעוד שמשתכר באומנותו, דתרתי בעינן: שמשתכר, ותפיס ליה אאגריה:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 81a:1:1.english: "I completed it" – a paid bailee - And if you ask: What is [the Gemara] challenging? Here it is different, for he is still holding the item on account of his wages, and therefore he is a paid bailee even though he has completed his work! However, according to [the Gemara's] reasoning above, where we liken a skilled laborer to a renter, and we do not say that a skilled laborer is different because he holds the item on account of his wages, [the Gemara] challenges well here. And one can answer that holding it on account of his wages helps only while he is still earning through his craft, for we require two [conditions]: that he is earning, and that he holds it on account of his wages:

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 81a:1:2.hebrew: לא הא הבא מעות וטול את שלך שומר שכר - ואע"ג דגמרתיו לא הוי אלא שומר חנם, לפי שנגמרה מלאכתו, מ"מ הכא שמפרש בהדיא שלא יטול עד שיתן מעות, הוי שומר שכר:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 81a:1:2.english: No, rather: "Bring money and take what is yours" [indicates] a paid bailee - Even though [with the word] "I have completed it" he is only an unpaid bailee, because his work has been completed, nevertheless here, where he explicitly specifies that [the owner] may not take [the item] until he gives money, he is a paid bailee:

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 81a:9:1.hebrew: אתא לקמיה דרב נחמן וחייביה - ותימה: מדלא אשכח לזבונא, משמע דלא הוי זבינא חריפא, ואם כן אמאי חייביה? והלא הנאת שניהם היתה, ואמרינן בנדרים (ד' לא:) דאין לחייב הלוקח אלא בזבינא חריפא, שכל הנאה שלו! וי"ל דזבינא חריפא היה, ואם היה רוצה לתת בדמים שנתן לו המוכר היה מוצא הרבה, אלא היה רוצה למוכרו ביוקר. ומה שלא מכרו כמו שהיה יכול, משום שאף אבבא דביתיה כשיחזור יתנו לו אותן דמים או יותר:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 81a:9:1.english: He came before Rav Naḥman, and he deemed him liable - And it is puzzling: since he did not find a sale, this implies that it was not a quick sale, and if so, why did [Rav Naḥman] deem him liable? Surely it was for the benefit of both of them, and we say in Nedarim (31b) that the buyer is liable only in the case of a quick sale, where all the benefit is his! And one can answer that it was a quick sale, and had he been willing to sell for the price that the seller had given him, he would have found [many buyers]; rather, he wanted to sell it at a higher price. And as for the fact that he did not sell it as he could have, [this was] because even at the door of his own house, when he returns, they would give him that price or more:
